title: Update on my MMORPG
author: iloveloon
selftext:
The game is [Piparune Online](https://piparuneonline.com/)  
  
I was prepared for a lot of backlash since the assets are AI, but the game has been quite well received in Thailand, Brazil, Taiwan, and Vietnam.

A YouTuber even made a [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UrHAiJP8Htw) about my game, and I'm very surprised that someone is that interested in it.

I use ChatGPT to create still images and iterate until I think they're good enough. Then I animate them using the MiniMax H3 model on [Mage.Space](https://www.mage.space/refer/BM74xqnAuvT8azdm0xNh4s17hlT2) (affiliate link)

comments.author: J0rdian
comments.body:
I run MiniMax H3 on my local computer and personally find the results generally much worse then what I get with googles video model using google flow. If you are ever having trouble with getting a higher quality animation that you want, I definitely recommend.

But I do also use Minimax locally for more placeholder animations or ones that I don't care much about.

Regardless looks pretty good, I like the updates

comments.author: CardstoneViewer
comments.body: Saw your videos on Facebook, thought it looked pretty great, reminds me a lot of a mix between Trickster and RO.

comments.author: DarkWaterWeb
comments.body: Wow! A youtuber reviewed your game? How did you advertise it?

comments.author: iatrik
comments.body:
Objectively, it looks great. Some minor things still look very "functional" instead of being fully polished. Like the cursor highlighting some kind of "square grid" or animations not tweening well into each other. 

Biggest critism are your "walk cycles" though. While all other animations look good based on what I see, walking looks really bad.  
And it's really noticable with how good everything else looks in comparison.

Play around a little bit with using anticipation for animations as a blending state into the new animation. Adjust walking, so they're not both "running" while also moving hyper slow.

Regards!

comments.author: FreeEye5
comments.body:
I think probably the 'Massively' part of 'Massively Multiplayer Online RPG' is probably where you're gonna struggle. These types of games live and die on their player bases all playing at the same time, which needs enterprise grade servers, etc, etc. 
And if you wanna chuck it out and try something else you can't say 'well I was just making it for myself anyway'
